'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[2025 Gaza City offensive]]
***At least 88 [[Palestinians]] are killed by the [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli military]] as [[Israel]] continues its [[Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip|heavy bombardment]] of [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://www.ft.com/content/75c1819a-9768-4914-be7f-705438c56b82 (''Financial Times'')]
***[[Ministry of Defense (Israel)|Israeli defence minister]] [[Israel Katz]] announces that the Israeli military killed [[Hamas]] spokesperson [[Abu Obaida (Hamas)|Abu Obaida]] in an [[airstrike]] on [[Gaza City]] yesterday. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm214r5rd29o (BBC News)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***At least seven people are killed and 71 others are injured in [[Shell (projectile)|shelling]] by the [[Rapid Support Forces]] in [[Al-Fashir]], [[North Darfur]], [[Sudan]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/seven-dead-71-wounded-as-sudan-s-rsf-shells-besieged-city-7e62f02e (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*[[Guyana–Venezuela territorial dispute]]
**The [[Guyana|Guyanese]] [[Guyana Defence Force|military]] report that [[Venezuela]]n gunfire targeted a [[patrol boat]] escorting [[2025 Guyanese general election|election]] materials on the [[Cuyuní River]] in the disputed Essequibo region. [https://www.trtworld.com/world/article/ac7bb99848a4 (AFP via TRT World)]
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
**The [[Houthis]] raid [[United Nations]] offices in [[Sanaa]], [[Yemen]], and [[2025 Houthi raids on UN buildings in Sanaa|detain at least eleven UN personnel]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/houthis-detain-at-least-11-un-workers-in-yemen-raids-says-envoy/ (''The Times of Israel'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Kunar earthquake|2025 Afghanistan earthquake]]
**At least 610 people are killed and 1,300 others are injured when a {{M|w|6.0}} earthquake strikes [[Jalalabad]], [[Nangarhar province]], [[Afghanistan]]. [https://trt.global/world/article/f56040733e07 (TRT World)] [https://www.thetimes.com/world/asia/article/afghanistan-earthquake-today-jalalabad-9h53wtjlt (''The Times'')]
*[[2025 Tarasin landslide]]
**Over 1,000 people are killed when a [[landslide]] destroys a village in the [[Marrah Mountains]] area of western [[Sudan]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2025/09/01/africa/western-sudan-landslide-marra-mountains-latam-intl (CNN)]
*Two people are killed and eight [[Kenya]]n [[Multinational Security Support Mission in Haiti|police officers]] are injured in an accident involving two [[armored vehicle]]s in the [[Port-au-Prince Arrondissement]], [[Haiti]]. [https://apnews.com/article/haiti-armored-vehicle-accident-kenya-police-695502533de8eda2d69c57f6110a4004 (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Armenia–Pakistan relations]]
**[[Armenia]] and [[Pakistan]] agree to establish diplomatic relations on the sidelines of the [[2025 Tianjin SCO summit]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1938704 (''Dawn'')]
*[[Norway–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[Norway]] agrees to purchase at least five new [[United Kingdom|British]]-made [[anti-submarine warfare|anti-submarine]] [[Type 26 frigate]]s for the [[Royal Norwegian Navy]] in a [[Pound sterling|{{GBP}}]]10 billion ([[United States dollar|US$]]13.5 billion) deal. The ships will be built by a consortium of companies led by [[BAE Systems Maritime – Naval Ships|BAE Systems]]. [https://apnews.com/article/norway-defense-navy-frigates-britain-b4dd3c7fc71fba6c13d1173237a21a4f (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)|Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip]]
***The [[Global Sumud Flotilla]], the largest civilian-led maritime convoy, departs from four cities in the [[Mediterranean]] and heads towards Gaza to attempt to break the Israeli blockade, carrying [[humanitarian aid]] and activist [[Greta Thunberg]] and actors [[Mark Ruffalo]] and [[Gustaf Skarsgård]], among others. **[[Philippine]] [[Secretary of Public Works and Highways|public works secretary]] [[Manuel Bonoan]] resigns over the [[flood control]] controversy, while [[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] appoints [[Secretary of Transportation (Philippines)|transportation secretary]] [[Vince Dizon]] as Bonoan's replacement.
